clauses.reason: Section 2(c) reserves to the President discretion, to the extent permitted by law, to depart from the order in designating an acting Secretary. It is a continuing reservation that has no end of its own; no held instrument amends or revokes it.

Section 3 provides that Executive Order 13242 of December 18, 2001 and the Memorandum for the Secretary of Commerce of October 3, 2002 "are hereby revoked". The order states no later effective date, so the revocation operated when the order was signed on 2012-05-21 (it was published on 2012-05-24); the command was complete on that day and is recorded as terminated by performance, with the revocation of the two earlier instruments as its surviving consequence. The actor is the order itself, and the source is the held original text of the order, whose section 3 contains these words.

research_rationale:
EO 13613 (signed 2012-05-21, 77 FR 31155, May 24, 2012) fixes the order in which listed Department of Commerce officials act as Secretary of Commerce under the Federal Vacancies Reform Act, subject to its exceptions in section 2, and in section 3 revokes EO 13242 and the October 3, 2002 memorandum. The held Federal Register text was read in full and its sixteen-clause inventory matches it (preamble, section 1 and items (a) to (i), section 2 and items (b) and (c), sections 3 and 4). The order states no duration or sunset. The three bounded searches (U.S. Code release point 119-121, eCFR and GovInfo CFR, and the Federal Register executive-order catalog) located no instrument that amends, revokes or supersedes it, and no held later instrument is attached. Section 3 is a self-executing revocation that was performed when the order took effect and is recorded as terminated by performance; every other clause is a continuing designation or limitation and is carried as operative on the original-plus-bounded-search basis.

savings.reason: The order contains no savings clause and section 4 disclaims any enforceable right or benefit, so no independent right or obligation survives apart from the designations themselves. The revocation in section 3 left no pending or accrued matter that the order preserves; the three bounded searches located nothing that preserves a residual effect.
